decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar, held in back to enter under Tailwind at eff. 400 Spe and Shadow-Tag-trap the board (Dazzling Gleam covers Scarf Krook/Hawlucha). Lead turn-one job: Incineroar Fake Out Venusaur (blocks Sleep Powder) while Noivern sets Tailwind; both resist Heat Wave so the sun lead can't punish, then Hurricane/sun Flare Blitz remove Venusaur. Garganacl completes as the Charizard-Y lock (resists Heat Wave, 4x Stone Edge OHKO, Wide Guard blanks Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide) and answers Krookodile
decisions.notebook: Durable reads for this series: Opp core is Charizard-Y + Venusaur sun; Krookodile (Scarf ~237) and Hawlucha (Unburden 374) likely, Sableye or Sinistcha as 4th. Verified speed tiers: Mega Gengar 200, Noivern 192; under Tailwind 400/384 beat Krook 237, sun Venu 290, Unburden Hawlucha 374. Pre-Tailwind, Krook EQ likely OHKOs Gengar — never expose Gengar before Tailwind is up; pivot via Parting Shot. Garganacl locks Zard-Y: sun Heat Wave ~21-29%, Stone Edge guaranteed OHKO (4x), Wide Guard stops Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide; Purifying Salt blocks Sableye WoW. Incineroar sun Flare Blitz guaranteed OHKOs Venusaur; Noivern Hurricane (2x) likely OHKOs Venusaur and Hawlucha (Sash caveat — plan follow-up). Sableye Fake Out can flinch Noivern pre-Tailwind; its Encore fails if target didn't move. Magic Bounce Hatterene reflects Taunt/WoW/Encore, Mental Herb covers the rest — hard TR mode (Hatterene + Kingambit/Garganacl) is the game-2 adaptation if Tailwind mode loses. Sinistcha watch: Shadow Ball 2x vs Gengar, Matcha Gotcha 2x vs Garganacl, Heatproof halves Flare Blitz, reverses TR; Kingambit Kowtow answers it.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Y + Venusaur is the strongest mode. Venusaur at 290 Speed under sun outspeeds Mega Gengar and Earth Power threatens OHKO (64-125%), while Charizard Heat Wave chips both foes. Sableye provides Prankster Fake Out/Encore disruption against Tailwind and setup. Hawlucha's Close Combat handles Kingambit and Garganacl, with Unburden speed as emergency control. Both back pieces resist Shadow Tag trapping (Ghost/Flying).
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent has Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag), Noivern (Tailwind+Sash), Incineroar (Intimidate+Fake Out), Kingambit (Defiant+Sucker Punch), Hatterene (Trick Room+Magic Bounce), Garganacl (Wide Guard+Salt Cure). Leading Charizard-Y + Venusaur sun mode. Venusaur Earth Power threatens Gengar; watch for Magic Bounce reflecting Sleep Powder from Hatterene. Garganacl Wide Guard blocks spread moves. Kingambit Defiant punishes Intimidate from Krookodile.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out must hit Venusaur: under sun it outspeeds Noivern (220-290 > 192) and Sleep Powder is the only way I lose control. Tailwind then guarantees Noivern 384 > Venu 290 for the t2 Hurricane kill (66-120%, Flare Blitz covers the low roll). Worst case incoming is Scorching Sands ~49% on Incineroar, healed by Sitrus. Tailwind also unlocks Mega Gengar (400) vs Scarf Krook later.

decisions.rationale: Sun from Mega Charizard Y doubles Venusaur's Speed to 290 via Chlorophyll, letting it Sleep Powder Noivern before Tailwind. Heat Wave chips both foes and breaks Noivern's Focus Sash if it connects. Incineroar's Fake Out is the only counter — if it targets Venusaur, we lose the sleep attempt but still set sun and chip. If it targets Charizard, Mega Evolution still happens and Venusaur gets the sleep off. Highest-upside line to deny opponent speed control.

Protect Venusaur from the double-target KO (Flare Blitz guaranteed OHKO, Hurricane 81-122% at 50% acc). Charizard Scorching Sands punishes Incineroar for 39-72%. Protect +4 priority ensures Venusaur shields before Noivern. This preserves my sun core for next turn while the opponent's Tailwind ticks down to 2.

reflections.summary: Won because the preview plan hard-countered the opponent's actual bring (Zard-Y/Venu/Hawlucha/Sableye): Incineroar's sun Flare Blitz OHKO'd Venu turn 2, Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapped Hawlucha and Zard (neither Ghost) while Dazzling Gleam hit Hawlucha and Sableye super effectively, and the Garganacl+Incineroar back-end cleanly closed vs Zard via Fake Out flinch + Stone Edge. The four brought and the Gengar Mega choice were correct for this opponent. Only real cost: Zard's spread Heat Wave doub

Opp uses Sableye Fake Out + Encore to disrupt and will double-target the fast threat (Noivern took Fake Out+CC turn 3); Encore can backfire if Noivern is locked into Hurricane into Sableye. Zard clicks spread Heat Wave even into resists — it double-KO'd chipped Gengar+Noivern; never leave both chipped vs Zard. Verified tiers: Mega Gengar 200, Noivern 192; under Tailwind 400/384 beat Unburden Hawlucha 374. Key mechanics: Hurricane 50% acc in sun — prefer Draco while sun up (turn-2 miss confirmed risk). Incineroar sun Flare Blitz OHKOs Venu (confirmed turn 2). Never expose pre-Mega Gengar to Krook EQ without Tailwind. Winning line: Noivern+Incineroar lead breaks Venu, Gengar traps and Gleams, Garganacl+Incineroar closes vs Zard. Game-2 fallback if Tailwind mode loses: hard Trick Room mode with Garganacl+Incineroar.

reflections.summary: The game was lost primarily due to an early misplay where Venusaur used Earth Power on our own Hawlucha, leading to Venusaur's quick KO and loss of our sun sweeper. This gave the opponent momentum, and their Incineroar + Garganacl endgame with Fake Out and Stone Edge easily cleaned up our remaining Charizard, which couldn't handle both threats.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, avoid such misplays and consider a lead that disrupts their Tailwind and Fake Out, such as Sableye + Venusaur to Fake Out Incineroar and Sleep Powder Noivern. Preserve Charizard for later and use Scorching Sands to threaten Garganacl, while playing around Wide Guard. If team options allow, replace Hawlucha with a Ground-type or a Pokémon that better handles Garganacl.
reflections.notebook: Opponent leads Incineroar + Noivern, using Fake Out turn 1 and switching Incineroar out to reuse Intimidate and Fake Out later. Garganacl is a bulky Rock with Wide Guard and Stone Edge, saved for endgame. Gengar is a fast special attacker. They did not bring Kingambit or Hatterene, but may bring Trick Room mode in future games. Our Charizard-Y must avoid Stone Edge and Fake Out; Scorching Sands is key. Venusaur is threatened by Noivern's Hurricane. Consider leading with disruption to prevent Tailwind.
